items.consigne: Read the short writing task. Name its audience and complete the writer’s purpose with “to + verb”. Give one detail the readers would need. Do not write a full essay.
items.stimulus: Task: “Write to first-time visitors of a pretend model-train display. Explain where the display begins and how visitors can follow the track.”
items.reponse_attendue: Acceptable: Audience = first-time visitors to the model-train display; purpose = to explain how to visit or follow the track; needed detail = the place where the route begins, or a clear direction along the track. “Model trains” alone names a topic, not a purpose. This preparation item is NOT one of the two mastery texts.
criteres: Names a reader group narrower than “anyone” and supported by the prompt.
Names a communication intention with a verb such as “to explain” rather than a topic.
Chooses a plausible, useful detail for readers new to the display.
Does not invent a required real-world fact or treat this short response as evidence of the full two-paragraph task.
items.feedback: If the answer is “model trains”, ask: “What do you want these visitors to understand or do?” If the audience is “me”, point to “first-time visitors” and ask the learner to restate it.
items.representation: consigne fixe en anglais, réponse courte écrite
items.variabilite_permises: Formulation personnelle et détails imaginaires plausibles seulement; lectorat, finalité, contrainte de tâche, nombre de paragraphes et grille inchangés. Aucun tirage automatique.

items.consigne: Make a two-box plan (paragraph one and paragraph two), not a completed text. Label the audience and the purpose. Show why paragraph two should follow paragraph one.
items.stimulus: Task: “Explain to a new pupil how to use a pretend class listening station.” Facts: headphones hang on labelled hooks; learners select a short story card; after listening, they return the card and headphones.
items.reponse_attendue: Acceptable plan: audience = new pupil; purpose = to explain a procedure; P1 = find the headphones and select a story card; P2 = return the card and hang the headphones after listening. Reason: the learner must start the activity before tidying up. Different but sensible groupings that preserve beginning → ending are acceptable.
criteres: Identifies new pupil as audience and “to explain” as purpose.
Places start-up information in the first planned paragraph.
Places finish/return routine in the second planned paragraph.
Explains a sensible order and records a plan rather than passing notes off as a completed two-paragraph text.
items.feedback: If the plan begins with returning headphones, ask: “What needs to happen first?” Give an ordering question, not a ready-made paragraph.
items.variabilite_permises: Formulation personnelle et détails imaginaires plausibles seulement; lectorat, finalité, contrainte de tâche, nombre de paragraphes et grille inchangés. Aucun tirage automatique.

items.consigne: Read two short paragraph ideas, choose which should come first for the specified reader, and justify your decision in one clear English sentence. Then suggest one sentence for paragraph two.
items.stimulus: Audience: children visiting a pretend puppet theatre for the first time. Purpose: to explain how a visit works. Card A: “After the show, visitors put their cushions in a basket.” Card B: “Before the show, visitors choose a cushion and sit by the stage.”
items.reponse_attendue: Correct order: B before A. Justification example: “Visitors must find a seat before the show ends.” Appropriate additional P2 sentence: “Then they can leave the room quietly.” A different relevant English sentence is valid. This is a sequencing check, not the complete mastery response.
criteres: Puts the “before the show” card first.
Puts the “after the show” card second.
Justifies the order by a meaningful temporal or reader-oriented reason.
Adds a comprehensible relevant English sentence for the second idea.
items.feedback: If the order is reversed, underline “Before” and “After”; ask the learner to picture the visitor’s steps and retry with no new example.
items.representation: two fixed paragraph idea cards plus justification
items.variabilite_permises: Formulation personnelle et détails imaginaires plausibles seulement; lectorat, finalité, contrainte de tâche, nombre de paragraphes et grille inchangés. Aucun tirage automatique.

items.consigne: Write a short two-paragraph guide in English to new participants of a pretend kite-design workshop. First provide a two-box plan. Explain how to begin and how to share the finished paper designs.
items.stimulus: Fictional non-flight workshop: paper kite drawings, coloured pencils, a display board; nobody uses sharp tools or flies real kites. The readers know nothing about the workshop.
items.reponse_attendue:
Possible plan: P1 choose paper / draw a kite; P2 display design / look at others’ work. Possible response: “Welcome to our kite-design workshop. You can choose a sheet of paper and draw a kite with coloured pencils. Think about the shapes you want to use.

When your picture is finished, put it on the display board. You can look at other designs and share one thing you notice. Please keep the pencils ready for the next group.” Assess by D1–D4 as a formative piece, allowing alternative clear wording.
criteres: Names or clearly addresses new workshop participants with an explanatory purpose.
Includes a two-box plan ordered from starting to sharing.
Produces exactly two linked English paragraphs with a visible break.
Provides understandable instructions consistent with the harmless fictional materials and shows learner ownership of the drafting.
items.feedback: If the two paragraphs both list drawing materials, ask for the later step: “What will readers do after they finish?” Invite the learner to revise independently.
items.variabilite_permises: Formulation personnelle et détails imaginaires plausibles seulement; lectorat, finalité, contrainte de tâche, nombre de paragraphes et grille inchangés. Aucun tirage automatique.

items.consigne: Revise this two-paragraph English message for a new pupil instead of a teacher. Show two specific changes and explain how one helps that reader. Keep two coherent paragraphs.
items.stimulus:
Original message to a teacher about a fictional classroom science tray:
“Dear Teacher, I request permission to access the demonstration tray. The contents are organized into three labelled sections.

I will ensure that all materials are returned to their designated storage areas. Kindly confirm whether this procedure is acceptable.” New audience: a new pupil who has already been allowed to use the tray. Facts: three labelled sections; materials go back in the same sections.
items.reponse_attendue:
Possible revised text: “The science tray has three labelled sections. You can look at each label to find the materials you need.

When you finish, put each item back in the same section. This helps the next pupil find it.” Explanation: replaced a permission request and formal address with direct, usable directions for a new pupil. Alternatives are acceptable if audience, meaning and paragraph order remain clear.
criteres: Keeps the two-paragraph form and preserves the fictional facts.
Replaces teacher-specific permission language with directions appropriate to a new pupil.
Makes two meaningful text changes rather than only fixing punctuation.
Explains why at least one change makes the message more usable for its new audience.
items.feedback: If the revision merely replaces “Dear Teacher”, ask: “Does the new pupil need permission, or do they need to know what to do?” Revise the action sentence.
items.variabilite_permises: Formulation personnelle et détails imaginaires plausibles seulement; lectorat, finalité, contrainte de tâche, nombre de paragraphes et grille inchangés. Aucun tirage automatique.

items.consigne: Write an invitation in two ordered English paragraphs for another class to attend a pretend shadow-play display. Write your audience, purpose and plan first; include what visitors will see and how they can participate.
items.stimulus: Fictional activity: paper silhouettes and an adult-controlled light behind a screen; visiting pupils may invent a story aloud; no real date, room number or participant names are supplied.
items.reponse_attendue:
Possible response: “Dear Visiting Class, our group would like to invite you to a shadow-play display. You will see paper characters tell short stories on a screen. We hope you can come and watch.

After the first story, you may suggest an ending for a new character. An adult will control the light while we share ideas. We would be happy to hear your story!” Appropriate plan: P1 event and invitation; P2 participation and welcoming close.
criteres: Audience is another class and purpose is to invite, not simply list shadow-play vocabulary.
Plan separates introduction/invitation from participation and ending.
Exactly two connected English paragraphs progress logically for unfamiliar readers.
Details remain within the stated safe fictional scenario; English is understandable.
items.feedback: If paragraph two simply repeats the invitation, ask: “What can the visiting class actually do?” Allow an original action sentence.
items.representation: invitation écrite deux paragraphes et plan
items.variabilite_permises: Formulation personnelle et détails imaginaires plausibles seulement; lectorat, finalité, contrainte de tâche, nombre de paragraphes et grille inchangés. Aucun tirage automatique.

items.consigne: Write two English paragraphs to a pretend neighbourhood play committee proposing a shared puzzle table. Present one reason and then suggest how neighbours could use or look after the table. Make a brief plan first.
items.stimulus: Imaginary indoor community space. Suggested object: a labelled table with puzzles made from cardboard; committee is fictional. Do not assert that money, space or permission has already been approved.
items.reponse_attendue:
Possible plan: P1 puzzle table and reason; P2 how to share and store puzzles. Possible response: “Dear Play Committee, I think our imaginary community room could have a shared puzzle table. It would give visitors a quiet activity to enjoy together. People could choose a puzzle when they arrive.

We could keep the pieces in labelled boxes beside the table. Everyone could help put the pieces away after playing. Please consider trying this idea.” Alternative supported reasons and suggestions count.
criteres: Addresses the committee and aims to persuade with a clear proposal.
Plan and two paragraphs divide proposal/reason from practical next steps.
Includes at least one relevant reason and a plausible use/care detail without unsupported claims of approval.
English sentences communicate the proposal clearly; learner writes independently during practice.
items.feedback: If there is no reason for the request, ask: “Why would this idea help a visitor?” If the committee is never addressed, ask the learner to review audience.
items.representation: plan et courte lettre persuasive en anglais
items.variabilite_permises: Formulation personnelle et détails imaginaires plausibles seulement; lectorat, finalité, contrainte de tâche, nombre de paragraphes et grille inchangés. Aucun tirage automatique.

items.consigne: Rewrite this information for a different audience and purpose: from an explanation for volunteers to an invitation for visitors. Produce a two-box plan and two new ordered English paragraphs. Explain one choice that changed.
items.stimulus: Volunteer note for a fictional mini-music display: “Volunteers set up three instrument drawings on the table. Then volunteers place a question card beside each drawing.” New audience: visiting children. New purpose: to invite them to discover the display and answer one question card. No live instruments, copyrighted songs or music recordings are used.
items.reponse_attendue:
Possible plan: P1 welcome visitors and describe drawings; P2 invite participation and explain question cards. Example: “Welcome to our mini-music display! You can see three drawings of different instruments on the table. Each drawing has something interesting to discover.

Please choose a drawing that catches your eye. Read the question card beside it and share your answer with a partner. We hope you enjoy exploring the display.” Explanation: changed volunteer setup instructions into second-person visitor invitation.
criteres: Explicitly changes audience from volunteers to visiting children and purpose from internal explanation to invitation.
Writes a distinct two-idea plan and exactly two ordered English paragraphs.
Changes language and selected details to meet what visitors need without adding impossible external facts.
Explains at least one deliberate revision and keeps English comprehensible.
items.feedback: If the learner only changes “volunteers” to “visitors”, ask: “What should the visitors do or feel invited to try?” Require meaningful restructuring, not a synonym substitution.
items.representation: stimulus anglais source et nouvelle production écrite
items.variabilite_permises: Formulation personnelle et détails imaginaires plausibles seulement; lectorat, finalité, contrainte de tâche, nombre de paragraphes et grille inchangés. Aucun tirage automatique.

items.consigne: INDEPENDENT MASTERY TASK A. You are writing to first-time visitors of an imaginary student-built weather-observation gallery. Write your audience and purpose, make a short two-box plan, then write exactly two ordered English paragraphs. Explain what visitors will see first and how they can explore the second part. Reread your own text and mark one improvement. No model sentences are provided.
items.stimulus: Fictional gallery facts only: Area 1 displays student-drawn cloud pictures. Area 2 contains cards with weather words and a space to draw a matching symbol. There are no real forecasts, measurements or location claims. Readers are children visiting the gallery for the first time.
items.reponse_attendue:
OPEN-RESPONSE SCORING ANCHOR — not one mandatory answer. Plan must order first display → second activity. Example only: “Welcome to our weather gallery. First, look at the cloud pictures drawn by students. Each picture shows a different cloud shape. You can compare the pictures as you walk around.

Next, visit the table with weather-word cards. Pick a card and draw a symbol that matches its word. You may share your drawing with a friend. We hope you enjoy the gallery.” D1: first-time child visitors + informative purpose. D2: plan and exactly two different ordered paragraphs. D3: clear, understandable English. D4: learner independently planned/wrote/revised, noting one change; tools for access allowed but no supplied wording. This is MASTER PROOF 1, not just a word-count test.
criteres: (D1) Audience explicitly first-time child visitors; purpose to inform/guide and details suited to them.
(D2) Two-box plan precedes exactly two ordered English paragraphs: cloud picture area, then card-and-symbol activity.
(D3) English conveys accurate fictional facts in connected understandable sentences, with local errors tolerated if meaning is clear.
(D4) Text, planning and one marked self-revision are learner-generated without adult-written ideas or sentences; permissible access tools documented.
items.feedback: Report D1–D4 descriptively. For missing transition, point to “first/next” as a concept AFTER the evidence and reteach order; do not insert the phrase into the independent submission. A second new attempt is needed after remédiation.
items.representation: two-box personal plan, two English paragraphs, annotated revision
items.theme: maîtrise A : information à des visiteurs
items.variabilite_permises: Formulation personnelle et détails imaginaires plausibles seulement; lectorat, finalité, contrainte de tâche, nombre de paragraphes et grille inchangés. Aucun tirage automatique.

items.consigne: INDEPENDENT MASTERY TASK B. Write to the planning group of an imaginary town square. Propose a small public story-sharing bench for children and explain how people could use it respectfully. State your audience and purpose, make a two-box plan, write exactly two ordered English paragraphs, and mark one useful self-revision. No model sentences or content hints are provided.
items.stimulus: Fictional scenario: a planning group is collecting new ideas for an imaginary square. A small bench could display cards with short original story openings. No spending amount, safety approval, schedule, personal identity or real public policy fact is established.
items.reponse_attendue:
OPEN-RESPONSE SCORING ANCHOR — not one mandatory answer. Plan P1 request and reason; P2 responsible use and closing request. Example only: “Dear Planning Group, I would like to suggest a story-sharing bench for our imaginary town square. Children could sit together and read short story openings from cards. It might give people a friendly way to share ideas.

We could keep the cards in a covered box beside the bench. Visitors could read a card, imagine an ending and return it for the next reader. Please consider this idea for the square.” D1: committee audience and persuasive purpose. D2: clear plan, two coherent ordered paragraphs. D3: readable, appropriate English without unfounded approval claims. D4: independently planned/wrote/revised, one change marked; accessible input allowed, content assistance not. This is MASTER PROOF 2, in a different purpose, audience and setting from task A.
criteres: (D1) Explicit planning-group audience and a real persuasive purpose with relevant appeal.
(D2) Plan and exactly two ordered English paragraphs, proposing a bench/reason and then explaining use plus request.
(D3) English is sufficiently clear, complete and appropriate for an unfamiliar group; fanciful detail allowed but no real-world approvals invented.
(D4) Learner supplies original language, plan and a marked self-revision independently; record accommodations but no content prompts.
items.feedback: Assess D1–D4 separately from task A. If the letter only describes a bench without making a proposal, explain “You described the topic; what are you asking the group to consider?” Teach and reassess with a new persuasive situation.
items.representation: personal plan, two persuasive English paragraphs, self-revision
items.theme: maîtrise B : persuasion à un comité
items.variabilite_permises: Formulation personnelle et détails imaginaires plausibles seulement; lectorat, finalité, contrainte de tâche, nombre de paragraphes et grille inchangés. Aucun tirage automatique.
